source.publication: 2025 Oklahoma Resident Individual Income Tax Forms and Instructions (Form 511 packet)
source.section: Form 511 lines 1-14 and 18 (PDF pages 42-43); select line instructions (PDF pages 9-10); standard deduction line 10 (PDF page 10); exemptions line 11 and the Regular exemption terms (PDF pages 8 and 10); Tax Table (PDF pages 27-38); Schedule 511-A (form PDF page 45); Schedule 511-A line 6, Other Retirement Income (PDF page 17)

worked: Federal AGI = wages (you) 5,350.00 + New York State public pension (you) 20,000.00 + IRA distribution (you) 15,000.00 = 40,350.00. Federal taxable income = 40,350.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 24,600.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Oklahoma starts from federal AGI). Schedule 511-A: line 6: you 15,000.00 in federal AGI, limit 10,000.00 - 0.00 on line 5 = 10,000.00, claims 10,000.00; line total 10,000.00; line 18 total subtractions 10,000.00 = 10,000.00. Form 511: line 1 federal AGI 40,350.00; line 2 subtractions 10,000.00; line 3 = 40,350.00 - 10,000.00 = 30,350.00; line 4 out-of-state income 0.00; line 5 30,350.00; line 6 additions 0.00; line 7 Oklahoma AGI 30,350.00; line 8 adjustments 0.00; line 9 30,350.00; line 10 standard deduction (single) 6,350.00; line 11 exemptions: 1 Regular + 0 Special = 1 x 1,000.00 = 1,000.00 (no one is 65 or older, 0 Special); line 12 = 6,350.00 + 1,000.00 = 7,350.00; line 13 taxable income = 30,350.00 - 7,350.00 = 23,000.00; line 14 tax (the projection's brackets as numbers; the booklet prints only a table and worksheets): 0.25% x 1,000.00 = 2.5000 + 0.75% x 1,500.00 = 11.2500 + 1.75% x 1,250.00 = 21.8750 + 2.75% x 1,150.00 = 31.6250 + 3.75% x 2,300.00 = 86.2500 + 4.75% x 15,800.00 = 750.5000; total 904.0000 = 904.00. Line 13 is under 100,000, so the form reads the tax table: row 23,000-23,050, column 'Single or married filing separate', PDF page 29, gives 905; expected keeps the schedule figure. Lines 15-17 credits 0.00; line 18 income tax 904.00. The pension is not on line 5, so nothing is claimed there and the IRA has the whole 10,000.00 on line 6. Had the New York plan been a listed type, the one limit would be used the same way, so the tax here does not depend on that reading.
accepted_approximations: The brackets are derived from the printed tax table and the 100,000-and-over worksheets; the booklet prints no schedule. Below 100,000 tax is figured on the exact income, where the booklet taxes each 50-dollar row at its midpoint and rounds. At 100,000 and over the single and separate worksheet starts from 4,562 where the schedule gives 4,561.50.

A pension from another state's government, New York State included, is left out of line 6 and taxed in full. Line 5's list does not name it; line 6 is a list of plan types and the booklet does not say which type another state's plan is (covers_unclear in the record). If the plan is a listed type, it qualifies under the shared 10,000 limit.
